chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Yahya al-Tawil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
God, the Mighty and Majestic, did not make the spreading of the tongue and the restraining of the hand separate, but He made them both spread together and both restrained together.

key_terms.كَفَّ: Restraining or holding back (of the hand/action)

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between speech and action in Islamic ethics?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of 'basṭ al-lisān' (expansive speech) is linked with 'kaff al-yad' (restrained hand), illustrating that eloquence and action are spiritually synchronized. This reflects the Shia understanding of internal coherence, where a person's verbal expression and physical deeds either both flourish or both remain constrained, serving as a diagnostic of their spiritual state. The hadith emphasizes that true eloquence is not merely rhetorical but is accompanied by corresponding action or restraint.
